functions.name: main

memory_operations.via: printf(buf) - format string argument is user input
puts(" is not the correct answer.")

functions.behavior: Allocates 32-byte stack buffer at [rbp-0x20]. Calls read_input(buf, 0x1f) to read up to 31 bytes from stdin. Calls check(buf): if returns 1, calls print_flag(); else calls printf(buf) with user input as format string, then puts(" is not the correct answer."). Note: init() is never called from main (no setvbuf/alarm in main's flow).

functions.name: check
functions.behavior: Validates that input is exactly 19 bytes matching pattern 'printf_?s_dangerous' where buf[2]==buf[7] and buf[8]=='s'==buf[18]. Correct input: 'printf_is_dangerous'. Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise. The rodata strings compared are at 0x402004='printf' and 0x40200b='danger'.

functions.name: print_flag
functions.behavior: Stores XOR-encrypted flag bytes on stack at [rbp-0x50] (key=0x9f at [rbp-0x15]). Loops over bytes, XORs each with 0x9f, outputs via putchar. Then outputs newline. Verified output: 'hkcert21{l3akinG_the_world_giVE_U_7H3_FLAG}'.

functions.name: read_input
checks: if last byte read == 0x0a ('\n'), replace with 0x00
functions.behavior: Calls read(0, buf, size). If the last byte read is newline (0x0a), replaces it with null (0x00). Does NOT null-terminate if input has no newline. Does NOT clear remaining buffer bytes.

functions.name: init
functions.behavior: Sets setvbuf(stdin/stdout/stderr, NULL, _IONBF=2, 0) for unbuffered I/O. Calls alarm(0x3c=60) for 60-second timeout. NOTE: init() is NOT called from main — it exists as a standalone function but main does not invoke it. This means stdout may be line-buffered (default) and no alarm is set when running via main.

attack_surfaces.input: buf (user input from stdin, up to 31 bytes)
attack_surfaces.operation: printf(buf) — user-controlled format string passed directly as first argument to printf
attack_surfaces.reason: When check(buf) returns 0 (which happens for any input not exactly matching 'printf_is_dangerous'), main calls printf(buf) where buf is the raw user input. This is a classic format string vulnerability. Verified: input 'AAAA%p%p%p%p' leaks stack addresses (0x7ffee9eff6a0), code segment address (0x4014f0 = __libc_csu_fini), and libc-related addresses (0x7d738d2a1380). The input buffer itself appears on the stack at a predictable offset, enabling %n writes. No canary, No PIE, Partial RELRO — GOT entries at 0x404018-0x404050 are writable.

attack_surfaces.input: buf (user input, 31 bytes into 32-byte stack buffer)
attack_surfaces.reason: read size (0x1f=31) is less than buffer size (0x20=32), so no stack buffer overflow. The read is bounded correctly.

attack_surfaces.operation: indirect control flow: check(buf)==1 -> print_flag(); else -> printf(buf)
